o.text: Borrowed from Russian артикль (artiklʹ), ultimately from Latin articulus (“a joint, limb, member, part, division, the article in grammar, a point of time”).
Morphologically from əkin (“plantation”) + -çi. Compare Turkish akıncı, Northern Kurdish akincî.
Borrowed from Arabic عَادَةً (ʕādatan), adverbial accusative of عَادة (ʕāda). By surface analysis, adət (“custom”) + -ən.
From Persian صنعتکار (sana't-kâr, “craftsman”). By surface analysis, sənət + -kar.
Calque of Russian бу́фер обме́на (búfer obména). Izafet II compound of mübadilə + bufer.
Borrowed from Russian агрометеорология (agrometeorologija). By surface analysis, aqro- + meteorologiya.
